Scope: group E of objectui#7759 — convert the five surviving `z.function()` mirrors to named refusal arms per the objectui#6124 ruling.

⭐ The declaration is `yes` because this moves a **published authoring face**, which is the ground director batch #112 put every mirror-moving proposal at `yes` on — ⛔ not because a widening tell fired. ⇒ `needs:contract-review` is now on **this card**, the dual carrier must AGREE, so **hang it on your PR too**. An in-seat ceiling-tier review is owed on your final head; ⛔ do not flip ready, ⛔ do not enqueue, ⛔ no auto-merge.

⚠️ **The claim comment is the carrier the enqueue gate reads, and its spelling is fixed.** `scripts/pm/check-clause2-carriers.mjs:751-752` requires a **line BEGINNING `Claim:`**, and the declaration must be exactly `Clause-②: yes` or `Clause-②: no`, unadorned, on its own line. This seat broke that earlier tonight by writing `**Claim:**` and `Clause-②: **yes**` — markdown emphasis on a field a machine reads is corruption, and the gate then reported not "this is wrong" but "there is nothing here to read". Recorded so it is not repeated.

⛔ Re-derive every line address on this card before touching anything. Tonight this seat has had card addresses rot twice (objectui#9026, objectui#8832), deleted out from under a card once (objectui#8811), and quoted one bad probe value into a card body (this card's own `ObjectGridSchema` offsets, flagged in place).

### The heal

Same shape as its sibling **objectui#9092**: the seat released the claim cleanly at wind-down but no pm-state went on in the same write, so the card sat in the ③ 析取 and was invisible to every queue. ⇒ `pm:queue`. `needs:contract-review` **kept** — a legal card-side intermediate state before the PR exists.

### Why `Task` and ⛔ not `Bug` — the discriminator against its sibling

⚠️ Its sibling #9092 is graded `Bug` this same minute, so the difference is worth stating: there, an author following a landed ruling is **refused by `tsc`** — a declared contract contradicted, with a victim. Here the five surviving `z.function()` mirrors are the **old spelling of a converted surface**: nothing is refused, no author is blocked, and the runtime is unaffected. ⇒ residue of a sweep, ⛔ not a contract violation. `Task`.

### Why p3

No user and no author is blocked; this is the tail of a completed conversion. ⛔ Not p2 — leaving it costs only that the surface has two spellings for one thing, which is a maintenance cost rather than a live defect.

### ⭐ The control that makes this dispatchable rather than a re-survey

The filer's own reading, and it is the reason this card needs no discovery phase:

> `handlerKeyRefusal(` already appears **8×** in `data-display.zod.ts` and **20×** in `form.zod.ts`. ⇒ the objectui#6124 sweep demonstrably **did** reach these exact files; these five are what it left behind. A file the ruling never touched would show 0.

⇒ a positive control that separates 「residue」 from 「unswept file」. ⛔ The round does not need to re-derive whether the ruling applies here — it does, and the machinery is in-tree (`handlerKeyRefusal(key, disposition, label?)` at `packages/types/src/zod/tombstone.zod.ts:109`, `HandlerKeyDisposition` at `:69`).

### ⛔ Fences

- ⭐ **A ruling is already in hand** — objectui#6124 (maintainer, 2026-08-30, Q2 → A with C), delegated by director batch #112: 「E 组由席位按 #6124 直接派」. ⇒ ⛔ no maintainer letter, ⛔ do not re-escalate.
- ⚠️ **⛔ Re-derive every address.** The filer says so in as many words — 「this seat has had line numbers rot twice tonight」. The counts (3 in `data-display.zod.ts`, 2 in `form.zod.ts`) are the thing to re-measure, ⛔ not the line numbers to trust.
- ⛔ **Do not convert a `z.function()` the ruling did not cover.** Five is the measured population; a sixth found mid-round is a separate reading and goes in the PR body, ⛔ not silently into the diff.
- ⛔ Do not close objectui#7759 — measurement-and-proposal charter, stays open and unclaimed.

`Size/model suggestion:` S — five call sites onto an in-tree helper, with the count re-derived first.

## Premises re-derived on `origin/main` at `2026-09-14T23:42Z` — ⛔ the dev re-derives them again anyway

The card says *"⛔ re-derive every address — this seat has had line numbers rot twice tonight."* It was right, and here is the proof, so the dev starts from a measured position rather than a rotted one.

⭐ **And one correction the card cannot make to itself: the title's "five runtime slots" is four.**

`z.function(` occurrences read **3** in `data-display.zod.ts` and **2** in `form.zod.ts` — 3 + 2 = 5, which is where "five" comes from. But counting *per line* rather than per file shows `:370` carries **two** occurrences, and the second is **inside the `describe()` string**:

> `…; \`z.function()\` encodes no parameter shape, so the member on \`DataTableSchema\` is the authority for it`

⇒ the surviving **mirrors** are **4**, and the fifth occurrence is prose — the very sentence this card's own item 5 tells you to check for survival. The card contains both halves and never reconciled them. **The deliverable is four conversions**, and item 5's question is about that fifth occurrence, ⛔ not a fifth slot.

⚠️ This is a figure, so treat it the way the card treats every other one: **re-derive it yourself**, per line and per file, and report both counts. If your reading disagrees with mine, yours wins and say so — three devs refuted this seat tonight by measuring something it had quoted.

⚠️ `data-display.zod.ts:250` in the card's warning has also moved: the two `retirementTombstone` rows are now at **`:285`** (`align`) and **`:292`** (`cell`). The warning stands — ⛔ do not touch `:292`, and ⛔ do not confuse it with the live `z.function()` `cell:` at `:199`. Note that this file carries **41** `retirementTombstone(` calls, so "a `cell:` line that looks retired" is a real hazard here.

## The ruling, quoted rather than summarised

**objectui#6124, maintainer ruling 2026-08-30 (Q2 → A with C):** replace `z.function()` handler mirrors with a **named refusal arm**.

**Director batch #112, delegating this card to the seat:** 「E 组由席位按 #6124 直接派」 — ⇒ dispatched here directly, ⛔ without spending a maintainer letter. This dispatch is that delegation being exercised, and nothing wider.

**The ordering rule that governs the work**, verbatim from the same batch note: 「我们的项目以 objectstack 协议为准,文档应该以实际实现为准。**协议不正确的应该先修改协议。**」 ⇒ ⛔ never narrow or widen a spec-declared shape locally in objectui; if you judge the protocol wrong, **stop and say so** — a spec card goes first and this card blocks on it.

## `Clause-②: yes`, and what it obliges

Declared `yes` on the card's own ground: this **narrows the accept set on a published authoring face**, which is why batch #112 put every mirror-narrowing proposal at `yes`. ⛔ Not because a widening tell fired — `SKILL.md:476` makes the criterion a disjunction and the accept-set limb is the one firing here.

⇒ I have hung `needs:contract-review` on this card, and the PR must carry it too. ⛔ **The dev hangs no label** — not this one, not any. Labels are the seat's alone (upstream defect objectstack#18181). A prior seat stripped the carrier from this card at `2026-09-14T00:38:35Z` (comment `5657454064`) precisely because it was an unclaimed `pm:queue` card; it is back now because the card is claimed and in flight.

## What is owed, unchanged from the card body

Its five numbered items stand as written — re-derive the population with `handlerKeyRefusal` as the firing control; convert with the **existing** machinery (⛔ no second mechanism, 20 call sites in one file are the house pattern); read each key's **TypeScript twin** before picking a `HandlerKeyDisposition` and say what you read (⛔ no disposition by analogy with a neighbour); a **firing control per key** — the refusal shown refusing by name plus a control key still parsing green; and item 5's question about whether the refusal preserves `renderCellEditor`'s parameter-shape pointer or strips the only place it is documented.

⭐ Item 5 is now sharper than when it was written: that pointer **is** the fifth `z.function(` occurrence. Whatever you decide, say explicitly what happens to that sentence.

Also answer the card's ⭐ on proposal F: decide **explicitly** whether fixing `FieldConstraintsSchema::validate` and `FieldConditionSchema::custom` discharges `form.zod.ts:800`/`:801`, and say which. ⛔ Do not leave it implied.

## Deliverable

Worktree → code → tests → changeset → push → **draft** PR carrying `needs:contract-review`. ⛔ Do not flip ready, ⛔ do not enqueue, ⛔ no auto-merge — landing is the seat's. Report structured JSON: PR number and head sha, every premise confirmed **or refuted** with exact commands, your firing controls, and CI as total / success / skipped / non-green plus whether the reported `total_count` equals the returned array length.

⚠️ `Test (shard 1/4)` in this repo runs against a 20-minute ceiling with a margin measured eight times this shift at `116 · 72 · 58 · 47 · 39 · 22 · 1 · −4` seconds. A `cancelled` conclusion there is **objectui#9499**, ⛔ not your diff, and ⛔ not something you re-run or fix — report it and stop.
